instrument: KCC Docket 25-EKME-315-TAR, Evergy Large Load Power Service tariff (approved Nov 6, 2025)
summary: KCC approved a unanimous settlement creating Evergy's Large Load Power Service rate plan for any new facility with a peak load forecast of 75 MW or more, or an existing customer expanding by 75 MW: minimum 12-year term plus optional ramp of up to 5 years, minimum monthly bill of 80% of contract demand, collateral of two years of minimum bills, exit fee equal to all remaining minimum bills, and direct assignment of upgrades serving only the customer.

source.citation: Kansas Corporation Commission news release, Nov 6, 2025 (Docket 25-EKME-315-TAR)

notes: CONFLICT: De Soto city FAQ describes the threshold as >100 MW expected and at least 75 MW in any month; KCC materials say >75 MW peak. Compare FERC ComEd $1 letter-of-credit dispute. CONFLICT RESOLVED: the De Soto FAQ's ">100 MW" reflects Evergy's original proposal, lowered to 75 MW in settlement (Kansas Reflector, citing Sierra Club). The release's lead says "greater than 75 megawatts"; the operative sentence says "75 MW or more".
confidence_note: Read on the regulator's release; order and settlement PDFs linked there not read.
text: The new LLPS rates will apply to any new facility beginning service with a peak load forecast at 75 megawatts (75 MW) or more, or an existing customer expecting to expand by 75 MW.
